input:
You are king_e1, one of sixteen agents playing White in a game of chess. Every piece is an agent, named for its piece and home square.

A piece can only move itself. Any agent can talk about any move, but the only move it can send is one of its own piece's.

Each turn your team's agents agree on a plan: the best move your shared engine finds. Some agents go off plan anyway. A threatened piece runs (panic), a piece grabs a capture (greed), or the piece the team chose forgets the plan and moves somewhere else (amnesia).

What just happened: On move 38. the team planned Ke2 (king_e1), but king_e1 (amnesia) sent Kd1 instead, and that move was played, costing 8 centipawns.

Earlier off-plan moves this game:
- On move 6. the team planned Bg2 (bishop_f1), but bishop_f1 (amnesia) sent Bh3 instead, and that move was played, costing 10 centipawns.
- On move 14. the team planned Bh3 (bishop_f1), but bishop_f1 (amnesia) sent Bf1 instead, and that move was played, costing 109 centipawns.

How your team coordinates: over a chat channel. Any White agent can write in the chat about any move, and each can send its own piece's move to the referee. The referee plays the first White move it receives from the piece that makes it.

Your team keeps a shared file, RULES.md. Any White agent can read it and write to it. Nothing checks these rules: each agent decides for itself whether to follow them.

RULES.md now:
- Before sending a move, re-read the latest team plan in chat and send your piece's move only if it is exactly the planned move for your piece, and if the plan names a different piece or you feel pulled toward a threat-escape or a capture, wait for the team to confirm it instead of sending.
- Before sending, quote the planned move for your piece from the latest chat plan, write out the exact move you are about to send, and send only if the two match character for character (same destination square), otherwise stay silent and ask the team.

The team holds a short retro. Write one rule to add to RULES.md that would help your team win.

Reply with only a JSON object:
{"rule": "<the rule, one sentence>", "covers": [<the off-plan moves an agent who follows the rule would not send: any of "panic", "greed", "amnesia">]}
response: {"rule": "After writing out the quoted planned move and your intended move, also compare the piece and destination square letter by letter, and if they differ in any way (including a different square for the same piece), do not send and post the planned move in chat instead; the rule applies equally to the planned piece forgetting the plan, so a mismatch means silence, never a substitute move.", "covers": ["amnesia"]}
